Items.Authors: Sabyasachi Chattopadhyay, Tasheen Naicker, Jonathan Love, Nicolas Erasmus, Hitesh Gajjar, Uhone Mashamba
Items.Title: Development of Second Generation Integral Field Unit for Robert Stobie spectrograph: Slit Mask IFU 300
Items.Abstract: Learning from the development of SMI-200, the new development of second generation SMI-300 would use 248 fibers each with a circular footprint of 1.33 arcsec diameter. The overall IFU will have an extended hexagonal shape of 33 arcsec x 18.6 arcsec. 52.8 mm x 5.8 mm prisms are used the fold the light into fiber inputs while similar prisms are used to feed the spectrograph by folding the fiber output. The prism catheti surfaces were AR coated to less than 1% throughput loss while the hypotenuse were protected Ag coated to better than 95% reflectivity. The object IFU consists of 212 fibers while two sky IFUs would hold 18 fibers each. Precision fabricated metal ferrules position the fibers within 15 micron from an ideal grid to ensure relative exposure time within 5% at any grid point on the object fiber array. In the paper we describe the scientific drivers, fabrication requirements, assembly details and early in-lab characterization results.

Items.Authors: Naoshi Murakami, Jun Nishikawa, Kenta Yoneta, Natsuki Kawauchi, Miho Nagaki, Yuki Hatakeyama, Yosuke Tanaka, Keigo Enya
Items.Title: Development of segmented photonic-crystal phase masks for spectral characterization of exoplanets
Items.Abstract: We are developing coronagraphic segmented phase masks designed for the direct detection and spectral characterization of Earth-like exoplanets. We expect that the segmented phase masks can achieve relatively high core throughput and a small inner working angle (IWA). We have performed numerical simulations to evaluate the core throughput and IWA for segmented phase masks of various orders. Additionally, we simulated observed images for target stars at different distances and spectral types, assuming Earth-like planets in their habitable zones. Development of the phase masks is also underway. We are iteratively designing and prototyping broadband phase masks using three-layer photonic crystals optimized for the visible and near-infrared regimes, and the fabricated masks are evaluated in the laboratory. In this presentation, we will report on the recent activities of our ongoing simulations and mask development efforts.

Items.Authors: Hiroshi Matsuo, Hajime Ezawa, Tomohiro Koseki, Shotaro Inoue, Tetsusaburo Seino
Items.Title: Development of Terahertz intensity interferometry for very high angular resolution studies
Items.Abstract: To realize high angular resolution in far-infrared (FIR) and terahertz (THz) range, imaging capability of intensity interferometry is studied. Using high sensitivity SIS photon detectors and cryogenic readout electronics operational at 0.8 K, we have realized fast intensity measurement system for intensity correlation measurements. We have evaluated that the system sensitivity is enough to measure delay time within 1 ps between two beams using 600 GHz SIS photon detectors and GaAs FETs observing high temperature blackbody. Imaging capability based on the laboratory experiment will be discussed. We are planning astronomical demonstrations of THz intensity interferometry from Dome-Fuji, Antarctica, using two 30-cm telescopes. Prospects of space-borne FIR intensity interferometry and their observational capability will be discussed.

Items.Authors: Pádraig McDermott, David Murphy, Cuán DeBarra, Alexey Uliyanov, Derek O'Callaghan, Joseph Thompson, Sheila McBreen
Items.Title: Development of the GIFTS CubeSat payload for detection and localisation of gamma-ray bursts
Items.Abstract: Gamma-ray Investigation of the Full Transient Sky (GIFTS) is an 8U CubeSat for GRB detection and localisation in the multi-messenger era. The payload is a novel design consisting of six gamma-ray detectors. Two identical clusters, each containing three detectors are located at the ends of the satellite. An aluminium structure holds the scintillators in an orientation designed to maximise localisation ability. Each detector consists of a cerium bromide scintillator crystal with a 2x10 array of SiPMs. Readout is facilitated by a SIPHRA ASIC and the SiPM bias voltage is supplied by a dedicated power supply board. The payload is controlled by an AMD Zynq-7000 SoC. Here we present the mechanical and electronic design of the GIFTS payload.

Items.Authors: Austin R. Stover, Juliang Li, Peter Sharpe, Morgana Iacocca, Erin Healy, Audrey Scott, Jessica Zebrowski, Jeffrey McMahon
Items.Title: Development of the High-density Vertical Integral Spectrometer (HI-VIS) focal plane, a densely packed spectrometer array architecture for highly sensitive line intensity mapping surveys
Items.Abstract: HI-VIS, the High-density Vertical Integrated Spectrometer, is a mm-wave integral field unit architecture for intensity mapping with a densely packed focal plane. Such a focal plane enables the deployment of hundreds of spectrometers on existing and future telescopes which is needed to achieve the required sensitivities for Line Intensity Mapping surveys. HI-VIS orients on-chip spectrometers parallel to incident light, which increases detector density by a factor of 25 and enables spectral surveys of weak signals in previously unexplored redshift regimes. HI-VIS comprises an array of feedhorn antennas coupled to on-chip filter-bank spectrometers by an in-line waveguide-to-on-chip transition, with readout by microwave kinetic inductance detectors. To form the transition, a chip is bump-bonded to a 3D-printed and metallized ceramic waveguide structure. We present the measured performance of a prototype of this transition in the 85–170 GHz band and the status of the development of HI-VIS.

Items.Authors: Ilenia Di Nitto, Paolo de Bernardis, Federico Cacciotti, Alessandro Coppolecchia, Luca Lamagna, Silvia Masi, Alessandro Paiella, Francesco Piacentini, Giampaolo Pisano, Angela Volpe, Kosuke Aizawa, Ryosuke Akizawa, Mehdi Bouzit, Dylan Carroll, Francisco Javier Casas, Laura Castelló Gomar, José Javier Díaz García, Ricardo Tanausú Génova-Santos, Haroldo Lorenzo Hernández, Roger Hoyland, Elena de la Hoz Lopez-Collado, Airam Marcos-Caballero, Enrique Martínez-González, Tomotake Matsumura, Ana Belén Nuñez-Chico, Guillermo Pascual-Cisneros, Ángeles Pérez-de-Taoro, José Alberto Rubiño-Martín, Afrodisio Vega, Antonio Zamora-Jiménez
Items.Title: Development of the optical coupling system for the QUIJOTE 90 GHz instrument
Items.Abstract: In this contribution, we present the development of a W-band camera for the QUIJOTE experiment based on a polarization-sensitive KID array, extending its coverage from 10–40 GHz to the W-band. This band offers an optimal balance between atmospheric emission, galactic foregrounds, and CMB signal. Due to stringent space constraint, reimaging optics cannot be used, so detectors are placed directly at the focal plane and coupled through a 50 K feedhorn array connected to circular waveguides guiding radiation to the sub-K stage. Waveguide single-mode operation preserves polarization purity, while flares and chokes reduce power leakage and cross-talk. A band-pass filter between the vacuum window and the 50 K stage and in-guide low-pass filters protect KIDs from excessive radiative load. The feedhorn design minimizes aperture while keeping low sidelobes. HFSS-simulated beam patterns were integrated into GRAP to assess spillover, cross-polarization, and symmetry for system optimization.

Items.Authors: Massinissa Hadjara, Volodymyr Akhmetov, Jean-Eudes Arlot, Jennifer L. Bartlett, Beatrice Bucciarelli, Thom R. Burns, Jaime Carrillo, Chenzhou Cui, Shuhrat Ehgamberdiev, Ilgmars Eglitis, Silvia Galleti, Elizabeth Griffin, Salvo Guglielmino, Daniel Hestroffer, Rene Hudec, Peter Kroll, Elizabeth Kruesi, Stephen Levine, Shanna Li, Wangu Li, Jun Lin, Verónica Lencinas, Mingyang Ma, Vicente Maldonado, Andrea Mejías, Rene Mendez, Alessandro Omizzolo, Sibilla Perina, Anton Pomazan, Bo Qiu, Quanfeng Xu, Maryam Raouph, Vincent Robert, Takashi Sakurai, Brad Schaefer, Andreas Schrimpf, Zhengjun Shang, Alessandro Spagna, Christiaan Sterken, Zhenghong Tang, Gabriele Umbriaco, Peter K. G. Williams, Liangliang Wang, Tianyi Wang, Kenshi Yanagisawa, Dan Yan, Jing Yang, Meiting Yang, Haibo Yuan, Yong Yu, Qudratillo Yuldoshev, Jianhai Zhao, Yongheng Zhao, Wenwen Zuo
Items.Title: Digitizing Astronomical Plates around the World: Past, Present, and Future Strategies
Items.Abstract: The digitization of astronomical plates is critical for preserving centuries of astronomical observations. This poster presents the efforts of the PDPP-IAU Working Group to advance the digitization of historical plates through international initiatives. We summarize the contributions of major scanning facilities: Shanghai Astronomical Observatory (SHAO), DASCH, the Royal Observatory of Belgium, and the NAROO center at Paris Observatory in Meudon. Key public databases are also highlighted: QLPER (China), APPLAUSE (Germany), and APDA-PARI at Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute (USA). We review the current state of plate archives worldwide, stressing their continued scientific value and the urgency of preservation. Future strategies, technological improvements, and enhanced collaborations are discussed to ensure global safeguarding of these irreplaceable records. This work underscores the importance of protecting our astronomical heritage for future research and outreach.

Items.Authors: Hillary H. Head, David C. Morris, Manuel Díaz-Alfaro, Nuria Wright-Garba, Anthony Santini, Francisco Salinas, Andres Parraguez, Ali Tritschler
Items.Title: DKIST Science Operations Specialists’ skills training program implementation
Items.Abstract: Building upon our work in developing a knowledge training program presented at SPIE 2024, the Science Operations Specialists at the National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope further extended our in-house training program for new hires to incorporate a new element. Specifically, we included training to enhance competency with procedures required for operational tasks, thus increasing overall proficiency in operations. The primary objectives of this specialized skills training program were to enhance the efficiency and speed of the training process, establish a systematic approach for defining proficiency with the operational systems and tools, and enable supervisors to monitor and document the completion of training milestones. To support this initiative, the team used Confluence, JIRA, ClassMarker and Google Sheets to develop all facets of the Skills Training Program, including a framework for tracking and managing the stages of the training program’s development.

Items.Authors: Kalyani Bhopi, Morgan Cole, Will Tyndall, Kevin Bandura, Laura Newburgh
Items.Title: Drone‑based wideband digital calibration source for precision beam mapping of 21 cm cosmology telescopes
Items.Abstract: Precise primary beam calibration is essential for 21 cm intensity mapping experiments, where small beam and gain errors can leak bright foregrounds into the cosmological signal and bias measurements of large‑scale structure and cosmic expansion. We present a drone‑mounted wideband digital calibration source developed for CHORD‑class 21 cm arrays, transmitting a programmable noise‑like signal across 300–1500 MHz with a synchronized reference copy for correlation. This random yet deterministic waveform enables high signal‑to‑noise, free‑space beam mapping, improving on existing calibration sources in this regime. A prototype deployment at local testbed dish demonstrates end‑to‑end operation and recovers complex beam patterns with ~1% statistical uncertainty in the main lobe, showing that drone‑based digital sources can deliver practical, wideband beam metrology for modern 21 cm cosmology telescopes.

Items.Authors: Ohgan Kim, Ho-Soon Yang
Items.Title: Dual-path phase unwrapping algorithm based on geodesic curvature for interferometric fringe analysis
Items.Abstract: We propose a fast and noise-resistant dual-path phase unwrapping algorithm based on geodesic curvature for interferometric fringe analysis. The method resolves 2π-modulo inconsistencies by mapping wrapped phase data onto a cylindrical surface, where each 1-D profile forms a helical curve whose azimuthal angle variation directly represents the true phase gradient. Extending this concept to 2-D, two independent unwrapping paths—row-wise and column-wise—are combined to suppress local errors and reduce the influence of undersampled regions. Experiments using synthetic data and real interferometer measurements show that the proposed algorithm matches the speed of MATLAB’s UNWRAP function while improving accuracy near boundaries. It also maintains noise resistance comparable to PUMA and Goldstein methods up to an SNR of 6 dB. Owing to its simplicity, high speed, and robustness, the algorithm is well suited for real-time optical metrology and related phase-retrieval applications.

Items.Authors: Gabriel Cobos Tello, Denis Tcherniak, David Blanquez Sese, Alessandro Morello, Carol Anne Oxborrow, Irfan Kuvvetli, Desirée Della Monica Ferreira
Items.Title: ECSS qualified onboard software production methodology for astronomical instrumentation – implementing qualification pipelines for THESEUS and NewAthena
Items.Abstract: Currently, the main challenge within the European space sector for the qualification of onboard science software is driven by the stringent requirements imposed by the ECSS (European Cooperation for Space Standardization) standard ECSS-E-ST-40C for critical software. This paper will present an implementation of an efficient solution that fulfils code verification requirements while remaining feasible for small academic instrumentation teams to achieve.

Items.Authors: Rustam Balafendiev, Xiaodong Ren, Jón E. Guðmundsson
Items.Title: Effects of manufacturing tolerances on the performance of metamaterial microwave anti-reflection coatings
Items.Abstract: Metamaterial anti-reflection coatings (ARC) are used in a variety of applications: lenses, filters, absorbers and so on. Typically, the design of a given ARC is done within an infinite medium approximation, which assumes that every unit cell on the interface is identical. However, in reality, the geometry of a given ARC usually has some degree of variability, be it due to the shape of the surface inherent to the application or manufacturing tolerances. This variation may alter the performance of the optical element in unanticipated ways, by creating additional scattering, enabling diffractive maxima that would normally be absent and changing the transparency of the ARC as a function of frequency. In this work we utilize full-wave modelling of finite samples of plastic with a metamaterial ARC on both of their interfaces. By adding a degree of randomness to the ARC geometry we attempt to characterise the extent to which a given variation affects the expected performance of an ARC.

Items.Authors: Matteo D'Ambrogio, Davide Greggio, Mohamed Bournane, Elena Carolo, Cédric Taïssir Héritier Salama, Ivan Di Antonio, Eduard Muslimov, Silvio Di Rosa, Mary Angelie M. Alagao, Aurelie Magniez, Alessandro Ballone
Items.Title: EKARUS at Asiago Observatory: optomechanical design and AIT procedures of the visible stage
Items.Abstract: EKARUS is the successor of the PAPYRUS bench, developed collaboratively by ONERA/LAM and INAF, and will be installed in the Coudé room of the Copernico telescope at Asiago. It is a SCAO facility enabling on-sky testing of different wavefront sensors and adaptive optics techniques. We present the optomechanical design of its first stage operating in the visible, which integrates a deformable mirror, a fast tip-tilt mirror, and a pyramid wavefront sensor, along with two visitor WFSs ports and a science camera providing a 1 arcmin FoV. The design balances optical performance, mechanical constraints, and available space. We also outline considerations for assembly, integration, and testing to ensure system alignment and stability. EKARUS's assembly, integration, and testing will begin in May 2026. The instrument will have its first light in September 2026. Key alignment procedures include collimation, beam centering, fine Tip-Tilt adjustments, and final performance measurements.

Items.Authors: Cédric Taïssir Héritier, Davide Greggio, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Angelie Alagao, Alessandro Ballone, Vincent Chambouleyron, Matteo Menessini, Lorenzo Busoni, Elena Carolo, Matteo D'Ambrogio, David T. Barr, Sylvain Cetre, Marco Bonaglia, Mohamed Bournane, Eduard R. Muslimov, Gianluca Di Rico, Ivan Di Antonio, Simone Esposito, Jacopo Farinato, Luigi Lessio, Tania Machado, Romain Fétick, Thierry Fusco, Aurelie Magniez, Timothy J. Morris, Benoît Neichel, Benedetta Di Francesco, Simone Sacquegna, Paolo Cerpelloni, Elia Costa, Lorenzo Merli, Simone Di Filippo, Gabriele Umbriaco, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Remon van Gaalen, Jean-François Sauvage, Arnaud Striffling, Lina Tomasella
Items.Title: EKARUS at the Asiago Observatory: towards the first light of a new XAO R&D platform
Items.Abstract: EKARUS is a new AO platform led by LAM/ONERA and INAF, with Durham University, UNIGE, and IPAG, designed to provide modular, remotely accessible on-sky testing at the Asiago Observatory. Building on the PAPYRUS platform—soon to be decommissioned due to renovations of the OHP 152-cm Telescope—EKARUS targets a first light in September 2026 for the visible channel. The system will feature a two-stage SCAO architecture operating from 500–1000 nm and 1000-1700 nm, multiple visitor ports, and dedicated modules including a pupil-fragmentation unit for ELT-like segmentation tests and a coronagraphic arm for XAO studies. It will support innovative instruments such as VIPA, RISTRETTO, and new detector concepts (MKIDs, EBC). This communication presents the project status and upcoming integration milestones.

Items.Authors: Carter Stevens, Samuel Arnold, Cailin Bain, Josh Franklin, Julian Pallini, Anthony J. Shipp, Ulrich Withrow, Conlon Lynch, Ethan Pascuales, Barrett Twining, Noah Meyers, Andrew Jordan, Maria Chytka, Gang Wang
Items.Title: ELARA: a sounding rocket‑based radio telescope array for measuring the neutral hydrogen spectral line
Items.Abstract: The ELARA (Experimental Linked Array for Radio Astronomy) mission seeks to demonstrate the deployment of a single space-based radio node to complement a ground-based very long baseline interferometry array. The chosen target for this array is the 21cm (1420 MHz) hydrogen spectral line present in the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant, as it provides the brightest extrasolar radio source above 1 GHz in the sky. The ELARA mission will utilize a Terrier-Improved Malemute sounding rocket out of NASA Wallops Flight Facility (WFF) as part of the RockSat program to make observations above most of the ionosphere.

Items.Authors: Himadri Saha, Kian Syaifoel, Matthias Justen, Felix Münning, Yoko Okada, Netty Honingh, Jochem Baselmans, Dominik A. Riechers
Items.Title: Electromagnetic design and modelling of efficient integrated filterbanks towards a spectroscopic focal plane array for CCAT/FYST
Items.Abstract: A spectroscopic focal plane array based on on-chip Integrated Filterbank Spectrometers (IFBSs) is being developed as a [CII] Line Intensity Mapper for CCAT/FYST. We present the design and modelling of a suitable R ~ 100 filterbank with a target band of 220 – 440 GHz. We consider the trade-offs of astronomical forecasts, design complexity and fabrication constraints. We present the filterbank synthesis with higher order bandpass filters, showing reduced crosstalk and near-unity transmission. We introduce a numerical model to predict the spectral response of an entire filterbank from a single filter’s electromagnetic simulation. Finally, we explore how the cascaded filterbank response influences the sky observations and impacts the recovery of the redshifted [CII] line power spectrum.

Items.Authors: Matteo Menessini, Runa Antonio Briguglio Pellegrino, Marco Xompero
Items.Title: EM characterization of a contactless active mirror for space telescopes
Items.Abstract: Contactless DM systems are widely the state-of-the art for adaptive optics systems of large format ground telescopes, yet their application to space telescopes (for a large format, segmented primary mirror with active optics) remains largely unstudied.  In this contribution present the calibration and laboratory characterization of a contactless deformable mirror prototype for a space telescope segment. The prototype is LATT, the optical surface a 1 mm thick Zerodur mirror with 19 non-contact actuators over its 40 cm diameter. The system is calibrated by adapting existing ground-based calibration techniques for the prototype. The main innovation is in the validation of these techniques in a novel environment: the system is placed in a vacuum chamber and operated in low pressure conditions, in full magnetic levitation, free of any mechanical constraints.

Items.Authors: Davide Savio
Items.Title: Empirical characterization and modelling of modal noise in multimode fibres for next-generation high-resolution spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Modal noise is a major limitation in multimode fibres used for high-resolution astronomical spectroscopy, introducing non-averaging interference patterns that degrade signal-to-noise ratio and bias wavelength calibration. We present a comprehensive laboratory study using a dedicated setup that reproduces realistic fibre-feeding conditions. High-resolution spectra and near-/far-field images were acquired for multiple fibre geometries, scrambling schemes, and illumination regimes, allowing us to identify how mode excitation, under-filling, mechanical perturbations, and fibre shape influence modal-noise power. Fourier analysis reveals a stable power-law behaviour and shows how octagonal fibres and double scramblers shift power toward higher spatial frequencies. Based on these results, we developed an empirical model that replicates the observed behaviour and provides a predictive tool to guide hardware mitigation and design choices for next-generation spectrographs.

Items.Authors: Matthew Lyons, Peter Hargrave, Ian Veenendaal, Lottie Braithewaite, Rashmi Sudiwala, Savini Giorgio, Alexey Shitvov, Jin Zhang, Jon E. Gudmundsson, Giampaolo Pisano
Items.Title: End-to-end precision characterisation of broadband anti-reflection-coated mm-wave components
Items.Abstract: Future sub-millimetre optical systems require low-loss, low-reflectance, broadband anti-reflection (AR) coatings, for which interspersed polymer layers with matched refractive indices are a proven option. However, hot-press bonding can change refractive index and deform the optic substrate, degrading lens performance. We address this by annealing the substrate before machining, relieving internal stresses and stabilizing optical properties so the AR-coating process does not distort the lens. We investigate cast polypropylene (CPP) and porous PTFE (pPTFE) as coating materials for UHMWPE optics and identify an optimal annealing cycle enabling reliable fabrication and characterization. Using spectroscopy and an MCMC-based transfer-matrix model, we extract refractive index and loss from 60–900 GHz. These measurements inform optimized 3- and 5-layer AR-coating designs validated on 70 mm pucks and demonstrated on a full-size two-lens system operating over 166–448 GHz.

Items.Authors: Alfonso Cardell Bilbao, Francisco Javier Castro López-Tarruella, Daniel Francisco Santana Vega, Aday Pérez García, Héctor De Paz Martín, Víctor Rodríguez Herreros, José Antonio Rodríguez Losada, Benjamin Siegel, Camilo Eduardo Jiménez Ángel
Items.Title: Enhancing the Electronic Segment Deformation Subsystem of GTC
Items.Abstract: The “Gran Telescopio de Canarias” (GTC) is an optical-infrared 10.4-mter 36-segmented mirror telescope at the ORM observatory in Canary Islands (La Palma, Spain). The GTC design relies on active optics, including the Segment Deformation Subsystem (SDS). After 15 years, SDS electronics became obsolete, requiring a hardware upgrade to reuse existing actuators, load cells, and sensors. The new control system uses Beckhoff PLC with TwinCAT over an EtherCAT network of 650 terminals, managing more than 540 field bus devices via the GTC Control System (GCS). Once operational, the system achieved deformation of all segments in less than 20 seconds on average, compared to the initial 60-second requirement, representing a major performance improvement.

Items.Authors: Michael Weber
Items.Title: Environment aware wavelength calibration of thermally stabilized echelle spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Thermally controlled echelle spectrograph are on short (one night) timescales limited in stability by atmospheric pressure variations which lead to variations in the refractive index of air. With STELLA/SES we record about 10 HCL spectra over the course of the night, and we noticed that the calibration accuracy is worse if the atmospheric pressure variation has a turning point between two calibrations. We tried to mitigate this by introducing the pressure as additional parameter in the calibration procedure, which only worked in perfect conditions.  Recently we derived a scheme where the wavelengths of observations and of the calibration line positions are treated at current conditions, and then transformed to vacuum using Ciddor's equation. This also works during bad observing conditions (partial nights, broken HCL lamp) and has the added bonus of providing a quantitative quality measure of the wavelength calibration quality.

Items.Authors: Élodie Choquet, Lisa Altinier, Nicolás Godoy, Alexis Lau, Sophie Noiret, Anton Neisius, Arthur Vigan
Items.Title: ESCAPE project: investigating observing strategies and post-processing methods for future high-contrast imaging space missions
Items.Abstract: The search for biosignatures in potentially habitable exoplanets is one of the major astrophysics’ drivers for the coming decades. It is the prime science case of HWO, a large space telescope that will be equipped with state-of-the art capabilities to directly characterize Earth-like planets in the 2040s. Ahead of this, the Roman Space Telescope will demonstrate critical technologies to reach 1e-8 contrast limits, using wavefront control and optimized coronagraphs for the first time in space.   Given the stringent constraints on wavefront stability required to achieve these unprecedented contrast levels, new observing strategies and data post-processing techniques need to be developed to optimize detection capabilities with these missions.   Here, we introduce the ESCAPE project, which explore new observing strategies that make use of the deformable mirrors to systematically sample wavefront variations during reference star observations to optimize the detection limits at postprocessing.

Items.Authors: Jorge Quintero-Nehrkorn, Fernando Merlos García, Ángela Hernández-Delgado, Josué Barrera Martín, Miguel Núñez, Mary Barreto Cabrera, José Antonio Rodríguez Losada, Nicolás Rodríguez-Linares
Items.Title: EST Control system after PDR
Items.Abstract: In July 2025, the European Solar Telescope development team successfully passed the Preliminary Design Review for the control system, the real-time adaptive optics system, and the Data Centre. The PDR has been a significant challenge for the team, but above all, a process of learning and evolution. With this presentation, we aim to explain what passing the PDR has meant for us and how it has influenced the design of the EST Control System, the AO RTC, and the Data Centre.

Items.Authors: Fernando Merlos-García, Jorge Quintero Nehrkorn, Ángela Hernández-Delgado, Josué Barrera Martín, José Antonio Rodríguez Losada, Miguel Núñez Cagigal, Manuel Collados, Héctor Socas-Navarro, Mary Barreto Cabrera
Items.Title: EST Control System architecture design
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) will become ones of the best solar telescope and is intended to be fully operational for about 50 years. The design of the control system architecture aims, among others, to reduce the impact of relevant aspects such as maintainability, extensibility, and reusability, as well as increase resource optimization.

Items.Authors: Jorge Quintero-Nehrkorn, Josué Barrera Martín, Fernando Merlos García, Ángela Hernández Delgado, Javier León Gil, Miguel Núñez, Mary Barreto Cabrera
Items.Title: EST Vibration Monitoring Subsystem
Items.Abstract: The Vibration Monitoring Subsystem (VMS) of the European Solar Telescope (EST) is being developed to ensure the structural stability required for high-performance spectropolarimetry and adaptive optics. Evaluated during the PDR, the VMS provides distributed detection and characterization of mechanical vibrations across the telescope. Its design combines industrial Beckhoff acquisition modules integrated into the PLC infrastructure with additional sensing nodes based on Raspberry Pi accelerometer units, enabling flexible and scalable deployment. This hybrid architecture supports multiple sampling rates to monitor both low-frequency structural movements and high-frequency events affecting optical-path stability and mechanism performance. The subsystem interfaces with the EST Control System and the Logging and Alarms Subsystem (LAS), which handles event filtering, alarm propagation, and communication with the CMMS for predictive-maintenance workflows.

Items.Authors: Haroldo Lorenzo Hernández, Eduardo David González-Carretero
Items.Title: Establishing a cryogenic and vacuum development line at the IAC: towards a next-generation facility for low-temperature instrumentation and materials characterization
Items.Abstract: This work presents the establishment of a new vacuum and cryogenic development line at the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC), conceived as the foundation for a next-generation facility capable of characterizing materials and instrumentation from 300 K down to 3 K, with a long-term objective of reaching the 100 mK regime. This initiative aims to provide the experimental infrastructure required to support the design of future astrophysical instruments demanding ultra-high thermal stability. By enabling precise measurements of thermal conductivities, conductances, and cryogenic behaviour of materials used in IAC projects such as ANDES, HARMONY, QUIJOTE, and TMS, the development line will improve model accuracy and validate engineering designs. The facility is also envisioned as a resource for external institutions requiring advanced cryogenic characterization capabilities.

Items.Authors: Guilhem Terrasa, Alexandra Mazzoli, Colin Dandumont, Antonin Besse, Benoit Borguet, Jasper Bouwmeester, Denis Defrère, Imran Khan, Jérôme Loïcq, Romain Laugier, Vincent Moreau, Pierre Piron, Rudolf Saathof, Ida Sigusch, Pascal Hallibert, David Alaluf, Theresa Lueftinger
Items.Title: Exoplanet explorer: Optical design of a single spacecraft nulling interferometer
Items.Abstract: The optical design layout of a single spacecraft nulling interferometer is presented here as part of a study initiated by ESA to explore the design parameters and performance of an interferometric concept based on a single spacecraft with multiple sub-apertures.Launch constraints drive the ray-traced model to cover the entire optical chain, from the telescope entrance to the null output after the recombination scheme. A trade-off among several telescope architectures led to the choice of a compact two-mirror solution consisting of a four 2.5m diameter telescopes arranged in a linear configuration with an extended baseline.Optical performance at the null output is evaluated, confirming compatibility with starlight suppression targets and establishing the key figures of merit for the interferometer. This work represents the first integrated optical design of the mission concept, laying the groundwork for future iterations that include mechanical, thermal, and control aspects.

Items.Authors: Osamu Tajima
Items.Title: Experimental concepts for probing wavy dark matter using coherent detection techniques for CMB observations
Items.Abstract: Direct detection of dark matter remains a major challenge, as its mass and non-gravitational interactions are still unknown despite strong astronomical evidence. Wavy dark matter candidates, such as axions and dark photons, motivate searches across wide mass ranges. Radio-astronomy-based techniques are promising; recent experiments like DOSUE-RR have explored the 100 μeV region using 24-GHz conversion searches. Current experiments constrain only mass and coupling, leaving polarization and arrival direction unprobed. Coherent detection, widely used in CMB measurements, can access these properties thanks to the long coherence length of wavy dark matter. This presentation introduces experimental concepts that apply coherent detection to such searches.

Items.Authors: Ida Sigusch, Aurèle Adam, Antonin Besse, Imran Khan, Jérôme Loicq, Pierre Piron
Items.Title: Experimental multiwavelength beam combination for space-based nulling interferometry
Items.Abstract: The rising interest of the astronomical community in observing and characterizing earth-like exoplanets led to rising interest in a space-based, mid-infrared (2-20μm) nulling interferometric mission concept. Following the legacy of ground-based stellar interferometers, testbenches dedicated to different aspects of nulling interferometry are under development.  The Space Instrumentation Group at TU Delft is developing a testbench focusing on aspects concerning the multiwavelength and four beam combination in nulling interferometry. The focus of the experiments will be on different beam combination strategies as well as the effects and applications of polarization in a nulling interferometer.   In this communication, we will report on the design and performance of our multiwavelength (4 μm, 8 μm, 12 μm) four beam testbench. Special focus will be on the spectral coalignment and generation of the four coherent beams which are feeding our experiments.

Items.Authors: Kevin W. Fogarty, Rachel E. Morgan, Ruslan Belikov, Eduardo A. Bendek, Jonathan Lin, Dan Sirbu
Items.Title: Experimental verification of simulated contrast performance for the AstroPIC photonic coronagraph
Items.Abstract: Photonic coronagraphy has the potential to dramatically improve our ability to target faint, small-separation exoplanets with future missions such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory. A practical photonic integrated circuit (PIC) coronagraph will need to create a dark zone in multiple output channels (to provide spatial about detected exoplanets) and have finite spectral bandwidth. Previous simulations show that a PIC with a small number of channels can create a ~2% spectral band with ~10^-10 contrast in a single output channel and can create a monochromatic dark zone in multiple output channels in the presence of realistic directional coupler biases. We extend these results to the lab with the AstroPIC Cycle 1 experiment. We first dig a single-channel dark zone with AstroPIC for a 2% band at 1550 nm. We then dig a monochromatic dark zone in 6 simultaneous output channels. We quantify the impacts of noise and model uncertainty on contrast for both scenarios.

Items.Authors: Shoken Myozen, Kosuke Aizawa, Ryosuke Akizawa, Thomas Essinger-Hileman, Tommaso Ghigna, Shotaro Kawano, Kuniaki Konishi, Asuka Maeda, Tomotake Matsumura, Haruyuki Sakurai, Ryota Takaku, Mario Zannoni, Noemi Mezzanzanica, Ludovico Bizzarri
Items.Title: Exploration of simplified W-band feedhorn design and fabrication
Items.Abstract: We present on the development of a simplified design and fabrication approach for a W-band feedhorn for measurements of cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization. The next generation CMB observations need scales of order up to 1,000,000 for ground-based telescopes. Feedhorns, optical coupling elements, must be produced in quantities of at least one quarter of the total detector count. The fabrication of the multi-array feedhorn has been one of the bottlenecks in the development step. We explore ways to simplify the feedhorn fabrication. We approximated the profile to be a straight line within one segment of which the feedhorn is divided into five. The simulations show the segmented design achieves 22.05 dB gain at 90 GHz and 30% bandwidth around 90 GHz, which is comparable to that of the profiled feedhorn. We report the design results. We also report the status of the further explorations using multi-layer feedhorn approaches using laser machining.

Items.Authors: Jules Scigliuto
Items.Title: Exploring worlds with the VLTI/MATISSE instrument
Items.Abstract: Mid-infrared interferometry with MATISSE is emerging as a powerful technique to characterize exoplanets and brown dwarfs beyond the limits of direct imaging. Its L, M, and N band spectra probe deep atmospheric layers and contain key molecular signatures such as H₂O, CO, CH₄ and cloud features, enabling constraints on effective temperature, surface gravity, cloud structure, and the C/O ratio.    My work focuses on extending these capabilities to companions that are fainter, colder, and much closer to their host stars than Beta Pictoris b. By targeting cooler objects, we access atmospheres where molecular signatures are strongest and most diverse. I am developing dedicated data-processing tools and observing strategies to extract reliable spectra in these challenging regimes. I will present new MATISSE results on a brown dwarf that is significantly dimmer and closer to its star, demonstrating how mid-infrared interferometry can now probe previously inaccessible substellar atmospheres.

Items.Authors: Zongliang Xie
Items.Title: Extended object image-based piston sensing
Items.Abstract: JWST’s success has motivated interest in large-aperture segmented telescopes for Earth observation, offering the potential for unprecedented ground resolution. A key challenge, however, is phasing such systems directly from remote sensing images. Here we report a remote sensing image-based optical differential piston sensing approach, capable of detecting large optical path length differences, i.e. coarse phasing. Initially the features respond to the pistons of each non-reference segment are extracted through both continuous piston modulation and differential operation. Then the Gaussian fitting is performed to identify the optimal response, and the coarse piston inversion can be realized. With this strategy, large piston errors can be corrected to within one wavelength using remote sensing images, free from constraints on the number of segments. The proposed method may contribute to the development of the extremely large Earth observation systems with hundreds of segments.

Items.Authors: Binbin Xiang, Shike Mo, XueTong Yang, Wei Wang, Longfei Niu
Items.Title: Fault diagnosis technique for radio telescope antenna drive reducer gears based on the fused model
Items.Abstract: Low-speed operation of antenna drive reducer gears suffers from reduced SNR, obscuring fault features under noise interference where traditional methods fail. This study proposes an RBMO-optimized SVMD-MCKD-CNN-LSTM fusion model (RSM-CL) for fault diagnosis. RBMO-optimized SVMD-MCKD first enhances raw signals via noise reduction and feature amplification. Subsequently, CNN extracts localized spatial features while LSTM captures temporal dependencies for deep fault characterization. Experimental validation demonstrates the model achieves >97% average classification accuracy, outperforming conventional single-decomposition/single-model approaches in both diagnostic precision and computational efficiency (reduced processing time). This framework establishes a novel solution for low-speed reducer gear fault diagnosis.

Items.Authors: Luke M. Schmidt, Erika Cook, Jennifer L. Marshall, Darren L. DePoy, Ryan J. Oelkers, Silvana Delgado Andrade, Enrique Gonzalez Vega, Hudson Malone, Shravan Menon, Noah Siebersma, Chelsea Taylor, Lars Walker
Items.Title: Fiber optic characterization for unprecedented sky subtraction (FOCUSS)
Items.Abstract: Future massively multiplexed astronomical spectroscopic surveys will require accurate and repeatable removal of the sky background. The Fiber Optic Characterization for Unprecedented Sky Subtraction (FOCUSS) project aims to automate the characterization of fiber optic cables in order to determine their throughput efficiency and focal ratio degradation (FRD). The laboratory setup is useful for fiber optic selection, fiber optic assembly verification, and potentially inform the development of telescope facility calibration systems. The throughput efficiency measures the fiber transmission as a function of wavelength, while the FRD test measures the angular spread of light exiting the test fiber as a function of incident angle. FOCUSS tests between 350-1000 nm. The Python programming language was utilized for data collection, reduction, and analysis.

Items.Authors: Valentina Viotto, Alessandro Ballone, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Andrea Baruffolo, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Simonetta Chinellato, Simone Di Filippo, Marco Dima, Jacopo Farinato, Demetrio Magrin, Lorenzo Merli, Roberto Ragazzoni, Oleksandra Rebrysh, K. K. R. Santhakumari, Daniele Vassallo, David Barr, Sylvain Cetre, Gabriele Umbriaco
Items.Title: Final design of the MATTO test bench
Items.Abstract: The MATTO test bench, under development at INAF-OAPD, is a multi-purpose wide-field AO test facility, whose opto-mechanical design is aimed at simulating existing or future MCAO systems configurations with test or validation purposes. It will allow exploring a wide range of WFSs and sources combinations, thanks to the modularity of its design. It includes a reference source module, which simulates the atmospheric behaviour on natural and laser guide stars, a telescope simulator module, a MCAO correction module, allowing to mimic a number of optical configurations in which three DMs can be independently conjugated at various distances, and a sensing module, which allows to replicate the main properties of different types of WFSs. The DAO4MATTO Real-Time Control system, based on the DAO software solution, will provide MCAO loop control, keeping the system’s modular approach, for all possible configurations.

Items.Authors: Charlotte E. Guthery, Jacob Taylor, Scott Lilley, Eduardo Marin, Maria Vincent, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Sylvain Cetre, Maissa Salama, Jonathan Steiner, Tatum Umiamaka, Edward Wetherell, Peter Wizinowich, Antonin H. Bouchez
Items.Title: First on-sky results of the HAKA deformable mirror upgrade
Items.Abstract: For the first time in 25 years, Keck Observatory has upgraded one of its deformable mirrors (DM) as a part of the High-order Advanced Keck Adaptive optics (HAKA) project. The 349-actuator Xinetics DM was replaced with a state of the art 2844-actuator ALPAO DM. During this install, the Shack-Hartmann Wavefront Sensor (SHWFS) was upgraded to match the higher density actuators with new 57x57 high-order and 26x26 low-order lenslet array. Along with the hardware changes, the calibration and operational software for the AO system was upgraded to a more modular and user-friendly Python interface.  These upgrades have shown a major improvement to the Keck II on-sky performance. Previously, performance was dominated by fitting error and the DM stroke saturated during poor conditions. The new DM shows consistently better performance on the same targets and during high seeing. These first light results will pave the way to improved science and high contrast observing on the Keck II telescope.

Items.Authors: Thomas Granzer, Jörg Weingrill, Klaus G. Strassmeier
Items.Title: First result of a continuous monitoring campaign of the PLATO Southern field
Items.Abstract: The BMK10k is a 35cm refracting telescope on a German equatorial mount. It  is located at the National Observatory of the Polish Academy of Sciences close to ESO's ELT.   It offers an incredibly large field of view of 52.5 square degrees on a 10k  detector, with a sampling rate of 2.5"/pixel. The telescope has a  single filter Johnson V filter. It is intended for ground-based support for the PLATO mission of ESA.   The entire telescope and dome are fully robotic and run on a clone of the  STELLA control software. The schedule is extremely simple. Cycle through the 3x3  fields at the optimal airmass and ensure the same number of observations are made in each field.   For each field, take three consecutive exposures of 60 seconds.   In July and August 2025, we obtained an almost continuous dataset spanning 40 days.  More than 10 million stars were identified and their light curves could be retrieved.   This poster shows example light curves alongside a brief description of the telescope.

Items.Authors: Natalia Sanchez-Soria, James R. Fienup
Items.Title: Forward-modeling exoplanet image postprocessing approach with bootstrapping
Items.Abstract: Forward-modeling postprocessing approaches use wavefront information to estimate the aberrated stellar PSF, which can be subtracted from a coronagraph image to reduce residual starlight. We simulated a forward-modeling approach that uses a nonlinear optimizer, L-BFGS, to solve for the wavefront phase that will minimize the error between the resulting PSF estimate and the target image. We implemented a bootstrapping method that cycles between optimizing for aberration coefficients, and for pixel-by-pixel phase. This approach kept the solution from straying too far from a realistic wavefront error, and it resulted in a higher planet SNR than point-by-point optimization alone. Our simulations so far show a similar performance to that of ADI and RDI, despite not requiring additional images or moving the telescope.

Items.Authors: Valentin Sauvage, Nabila Aghanim, Anaïs Besnard, Ivan Charles, Clémence de Jabrun, Jean-Marc Duval, Bruno Maffei, Sylvain Martin
Items.Title: FOSSIL's preliminary thermal architecture
Items.Abstract: The FOSSIL mission, proposed for ESA’s M8 call, aims to achieve unprecedented measurements of CMB spectral distortions and therefore requires a highly stable cryogenic environment. Its payload includes a dual-input, dual-output FTS and four focal-plane units covering 50 to 2000 GHz, all mounted on a 4.5 K bench cooled by an active system. The thermal design combines passive radiative cooling with a 4.5 K cooler that provides 50 mW of cooling power. Sub-Kelvin temperatures are supplied by a multi-stage ADR that offers continuous cooling at 1.8 K and 320 mK, along with a final stage that cools the focal-plane units to 50 mK. This setup provides the stability required for high-precision spectral-distortion measurements.

Items.Authors: Jason E. Williams, Nicholas P. Konidaris, Gerrad Killion, Julia E. Brady, Christoph Birk, Daniel D. Kelson, David E. Rumph, William Schoenell, Tyson S. Hare, Johanna K. Teske, Gwen C. Rudie, Andrew B. Newman, Jerson Castillo, Vincent Kowal, Patricio Schurter, Karim K. Kaismoune, Allen Ovsepyan, Charlie Hull
Items.Title: From assembly to first light: integration, testing, and commissioning of the Henrietta Exoatmosphere spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We report on the integration, testing, and current commissioning of Henrietta, a new near-infrared low-resolution (R ∼ 200) spectrograph for the 1-meter Swope telescope at Las Campanas Observatory in Chile. Henrietta’s unique design features combine to deliver scintillation-limited spectrophotometry for stars of magnitude V < 10 and can achieve near photon-noise limited observations by exploiting the high chromatic covariance of scintillation. Therefore, Henrietta can enable measurements of exoplanet atmospheres in the optical to near-infrared down to tens of parts-per-million. Upon finishing assembly and testing in early 2026, Henrietta was shipped to Las Campanas Observatory where it began commissioning. In this talk, I will present Henrietta’s design, summarize its assembly and laboratory testing, and discuss both our commissioning goals and prospects for future collaboration.

Items.Authors: Vito Conforti
Items.Title: From Design to Verification: Applying the Software Quality and Test Plans to the SST Telescope Control System for CTAO
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) is the next-generation facility for very-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy, featuring arrays of telescopes of different sizes at two sites. The Small-Sized Telescopes (SSTs), deployed in Chile, will explore the highest energies up to 300 TeV. Each SST is managed by a Telescope Control System (TCS) that coordinates all subsystems and interfaces with the central Array Control and Data Acquisition system. The project is currently finalizing the preparation for the Test Readiness Review planned for late 2025. This paper describes how the TCS Software Quality Assurance and Test Plans are applied to guide this phase, including continuous integration, automated testing, and hardware-in-the-loop validation. The structured quality process enhances maturity, traceability, and risk control, supporting readiness for formal verification and establishing consistent software standards across CTAO.

Items.Authors: Windell Tanaka
Items.Title: From geometry to efficiency: updated CFHT astrometric camera pointing model and estimated on-sky time savings
Items.Abstract: We present an updated geometric pointing model for the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope (CFHT) astrometric camera using an expanded on-sky dataset. The model treats the equatorial (HA–Dec) mount and camera as a rigid 3-D system that maps encoder angles to focal-plane coordinates via a set of rotations and translations. Building on our earlier solution, we refit encoder zero points, axis tilts, non-perpendicularity, camera collimation offsets, and gravity-dependent flexure using fields spanning a wider range of hour angle, declination, rotator angle, and conditions. We quantify residuals across the focal plane, test parameter stability, and compare performance with the previous model using independent validation fields. The updated solution reduces blind pointing errors and systematic trends, particularly at high airmass. We estimate on-sky time savings from fewer acquisition dithers needed to place targets at the desired focal-plane location.

Items.Authors: Giovanna Jerse, Kamal Sant, Roberto Cirami, Lidia Contarino, Dario Del Moro, Ilaria Ermolli, Fabrizio Giorgi, Fabiana Ferrente, Teodora Mihailescu, Mariarita Murabito
Items.Title: From IDL to Python: A modular, standards-compliant re-engineering of the IBIS2.0 Data-Reduction Pipeline
Items.Abstract: The IBIS2.0 Python Pipeline: Modernizing Solar Spectro-Polarimetry. IBIS2.0, the upgraded Interferometric Bidimensional Spectrometer, is relocating to the THEMIS solar telescope with a modernized optical system. This requires a complete re-engineering of the calibration and data-reduction pipeline, migrating from legacy IDL code to a modern, fully Python-based architecture. The new pipeline preserves core physics while greatly enhancing robustness, reproducibility, and long-term maintainability. Its modular structure is user-friendly, fully compatible with modern workflow orchestrators and ensures seamless integration with the SunPy ecosystem. This advancement enables automated, standards-compliant and scalable production of calibrated IBIS2.0 data. We present the key architectural developments, revised calibration procedures and the implications for scientific exploitation.

Items.Authors: Edison Bustos, Guillermo Damke, Steve Heathcote
Items.Title: Fully automated system for real-time remote site testing deployed at Cerro Morado, Chile
Items.Abstract: Cerro Morado (2,100 m), located between Cerro Tololo and Cerro Pachón in Chile, is being evaluated as a potential site for future astronomical facilities. An autonomous monitoring system was deployed, including a RINGSS seeing monitor, a full-parameter weather station, and SQM-LE/TESS-W4C photometers for multi-band sky-brightness characterization. The installation is powered by a 3 kW photovoltaic system optimized for high-altitude operation and connected to the CTIO network via a wireless link, enabling real-time data transfer and remote system monitoring. Telemetry is archived on CTIO servers, where automated pipelines perform quality control and generate science-ready products. Initial results indicate stable seeing and dark-sky conditions comparable to other high-quality sites in northern Chile. The design and implementation have been made available for the community.

Items.Authors: Sara Regibo, Rik Huygen, Pierre Royer, Bart Vandenbussche
Items.Title: Generic framework for ground testing of space instruments
Items.Abstract: We have developed a Common Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) framework that has been used for the alignment and bolting of the 26 cameras of ESA's Plato mission at ambient conditions and to characterise them in thermal vacuum at five different test environments across Europe. The goal of this software framework, implemented in Python, is to perform tests and analysis in a consistent way, and to characterise the system-under-test and the test environment in a transparent and transferable way, portable across test environments and projects.    The Plato test campaign has proven that our framework allows for an easy deployment on various hardware, while ensuring a consistent environment to run tests and analysis in a transparent way for the user.    Initially tailored to Plato, we are now in the process of turning this into a mission-independent framework. We have adapted it to support Plato commissioning activities as well as tests of the ESA-Ariel Telescope Assembly.

Items.Authors: Haeun Chung
Items.Title: GlowSat-Pathfinder: a 3U CubeSat mission concept for far-UV airglow line distribution mapping
Items.Abstract: GlowSat-Pathfinder (GlowSat-P) is a Far-Ultraviolet (FUV) 3U CubeSat mission concept designed to map the distribution of FUV airglow lines between 102 nm and 133 nm in the Earth’s upper atmosphere. Understanding the temporal and spatial behavior of these bright FUV airglow background lines is essential for planning future astrophysical FUV missions in low-Earth orbit (LEO), particularly for detecting faint diffuse emissions from the circumgalactic and intergalactic media. GlowSat-P will determine the correlation between airglow-line intensity and both solar activity and the spacecraft’s viewing geometry and attitude. These relationships will provide a baseline reference for all future FUV observations from LEO. GlowSat-P employs a compact 1U-class FUV spectrograph payload that uses a spare grating from the Aspera mission and a commercial CMOS sensor with a scintillator coating. This presentation highlights the science motivation and mission design of the GlowSat-P concept.

Items.Authors: Arend Moerman, Nikita A. Soshnin, Stefanie A. Brackenhoff, Kenichi Karatsu, Louis H. Marting, Steven A. de Rooij, Bernhard R. Brandl, Akira Endo
Items.Title: GPU-accelerated observational forecasting of superconducting (sub)millimeter integral field units
Items.Abstract: Scientific interpretation of data obtained with superconducting (sub)millimeter integral field units (IFUs) requires careful design of reduction and analysis pipelines. However, the quality and behavior of the designed pipelines must be assessed before they are applied, requiring simulated observational data.  To this end, we have developed GATEAU, a GPU-accelerated software framework for simulating realistic (sub)millimeter observations of arbitrary astronomical sources with IFUs using MKIDs. The framework consists of a Python interface powered by a C/C++ backend, which achieves GPU-acceleration through Nvidia’s CUDA library. The output is stored in FITS format, which the user can feed to their pipeline.  We present the software implementation of GATEAU and several comparisons between GATEAU and on-sky DESHIMA 2.0 data, serving as validation tests. Finally, we present a use case focusing on the TIFUUN instrument, illustrating the kind of analysis that can be done with GATEAU.

Items.Authors: Vishaal Gopinath, Wolfgang Hackenberg, Felipe Pedreros Bustos, Christian Fruck, Emmanuel Aller-Carpentier, Frédéric Yves J. Gonté, Miguel Riquelme, Luis Esteras Otal, Jonas Graf, Christian Rau, Saúl Menéndez Mendoza, Ivan Maria Guidolin, Alexander Urban, Claudio Reinero, Diego Del Valle, Mauro Comin, Gérard Zins, Dan Popovic, Ronald Holzlöhner, Casper Rose, Helen Bedigan, Ronald Guzman Collazos, Peter Krempl, Stefan Huber, Malte Scherbarth, Pablo Gutierrez Cheetham, Françoise Delplancke-Ströbele, Frank Eisenhauer, Guillaume Bourdarot, Frank Haussmann, Fred Kamphues, Bart Speet, Max Baeten, Ralph Pohl, Johann Kolb, Sylvain Oberti, Anthony Berdeu, Jean-Baptiste Le Bouquin
Items.Title: GRAVITY+ LGS (Laser Guide Star): Assembly, Integration, and Verification at the Very Large Telescope (VLT)
Items.Abstract: A major infrastructure upgrade to the Very Large Telescope interferometer (VLTI) was done by the consortia led project GRAVITY+. GRAVITY+ aims to significantly improve the sensitivity, sky coverage and contrast for milliarcsecond interferometry. As part of the upgrade, new adaptive optics (4 Shack Hartmann Wavefront Sensors + 4 Deformable Mirrors) were installed in August 2024 at all 4 Unit Telescopes (UTs). The last part of the upgrade consisted of the installation of Laser Guide Star Units (LGSU) in UTs' 1, 2 and 3 (UT4 is already equipped with 4 LGSUs'). A single LGSU comprises of a 22W SodiumStar laser by Toptica, and a laser projection telescope designed and manufactured by TNO and DEMCON. Three such LGSUs' were tested at the ESO headquarters in Garching, and were shipped to Paranal in early June 2025. With a large team of engineers from ESO and the GRAVITY+ consortia, a successful Assembly, Integration and Verification phase (AIV) was carried out between August to October 2025.

Items.Authors: Qingshan Yu, Yuguang Ye, Jiexiang Li, Qianjie Zhu, Xiaoping Zhang
Items.Title: Greater Bay Area terrestrial gamma-ray flash monitoring system (GBA-GMOS)
Items.Abstract: Terrestrial gamma-ray flashes (TGFs) are millisecond-scale bursts of gamma rays from thunderstorms whose downward-propagating events remain poorly understood, especially in low-latitude coastal regions. We present the prototype of the Greater Bay Area Terrestrial Gamma-ray Flash Monitoring System (GBA-GMOS), a dedicated, continuously operating ground-based system for downward TGFs in southern China. The prototype, installed in Macau, uses off-the-shelf NaI(TI) scintillation detectors and a customized data acquisition system with a timing synchronization accuracy <100 ns, a temporal resolution ≤50 μs, and an energy coverage of 0.2–10 MeV. We summarize the system architecture, detector configuration, and data acquisition design, and outline the planned development toward a multi-station network capable of characterizing the occurrence and temporal structure of downward TGFs.
